developerConsole: https://developers.hubspot.com (then Development > Projects in your HubSpot account; apps are created with the HubSpot CLI: hs project create / hs project upload)

composio.note: Composio lists HubSpot under Composio-managed OAuth. Use your own app for your own branding, a custom scope set, or install-count independence. The composio.dev/auth/hubspot guide describes the old 'Apps > Create App' UI. HubSpot disabled that for legacy public apps by 23 June 2026, so new apps must be Projects-based (CLI). Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

summary: Getting OAuth credentials is quick and free, but new apps must now be built as Developer Platform 'projects' with the HubSpot CLI. The old click-through app creation is gone. An unlisted marketplace-distribution app is hard-capped at 25 installs (a private-distribution app at 10 allowlisted accounts) until it is approved for the HubSpot Marketplace. Listing needs 3 active, unaffiliated installs and a review that can run up to about 60 days.
difficultyReason: CLI/config-file setup instead of a web form. The hard 25-install cap means any product with more than a handful of customers has to go through Marketplace review. AI connectors face an extra rule: they must use user-level permissions.

time.notes: Up to 25 accounts can install an unlisted marketplace-distribution app immediately. Lifting the cap needs 3 active unaffiliated installs, then Marketplace review: initial review within 10 business days, full process up to 60 days from feedback. The 1-3 month total is inferred.

review.details: You need no review to create the app and install it in up to 25 accounts (marketplace distribution) or 10 allowlisted accounts (private distribution). Going past 25 requires a Marketplace listing reviewed by HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team: 3+ active installs in unaffiliated production accounts, live privacy policy/ToS/support/setup-doc URLs, a scope-accurate shared-data table, and OAuth as the only auth method. Only one app per developer can be under review at a time. App Certification is a separate, later program that I did not research here.

limitsBeforeApproval: Marketplace-distribution OAuth app: up to 25 installs (developer test accounts excluded) until the listing is approved. Private-distribution OAuth app: up to 10 allowlisted accounts. Static-token app: 1 standard account. The installing user must be a Super Admin or have the HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.

prerequisites.item: Free HubSpot developer account (or a HubSpot account with Development > Projects access)
prerequisites.why: Apps are created and owned in a HubSpot account. A developer account also gives you developer test accounts, which don't count toward install caps.

prerequisites.item: Node.js + HubSpot CLI (docs call for v7.6.0+), authenticated with hs account auth
prerequisites.why: Developer Platform apps are created and deployed via hs project create / hs project upload. Legacy UI app creation was disabled in 2026.

prerequisites.item: Redirect URI from the Composio dashboard
prerequisites.why: It goes in redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json, and HubSpot validates redirect_uri against it.

prerequisites.item: Live privacy policy, Terms of Service, support contact and public setup documentation
prerequisites.why: Required for a Marketplace listing, which is the only way past the 25-install cap.

prerequisites.item: 3 active installs in production HubSpot accounts unaffiliated with your company
prerequisites.why: Minimum to submit a Marketplace listing. 'Active' means successful app activity in the past 30 days.

steps.title: Create or sign in to a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free developer account at developers.hubspot.com. Optionally create a developer test account for installs that don't count toward caps.

steps.title: Install and authenticate the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: npm install -g @hubspot/cli@latest, then hs account auth (opens a browser to generate a personal access key).

steps.title: Pick scopes
steps.detail: Map the Composio HubSpot actions you need to HubSpot scopes. Use requiredScopes for the core set and optionalScopes for tier-dependent ones, because missing required scopes block install on lower-tier accounts. Remove anything unused; Marketplace review rejects unused scopes.

steps.title: Scaffold the project
steps.detail: Run hs project create, choose App, distribution 'marketplace' (or 'private' if you will only ever serve 10 or fewer known accounts), and auth type OAuth.

steps.title: Fill app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: Set the app name, uid, auth.type 'oauth', the redirectUrls entry from the Composio dashboard, and requiredScopes/optionalScopes. An agent can write this file directly.

steps.title: Upload the project
steps.detail: Run hs project upload to build and deploy. Re-run it after any change to scopes or redirect URLs.

steps.title: Copy credentials into Composio
steps.detail: Run hs project open, click the app, then the Auth tab, and copy the Client ID and Client secret. In Composio, Create Auth Config > HubSpot > OAuth2 with your own credentials, paste both, match the scopes, save, and store the ac_... ID.

steps.title: Verify config and test-connect
steps.detail: Check that the redirect URL and scopes in app-hsmeta.json match Composio. Then connect a developer test account through Composio and confirm the granted scopes on the token.

steps.title: Approve install in a real account
steps.detail: A Super Admin (or user with Marketplace Access permission) in the target HubSpot account completes the consent screen.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace listing (only if you need more than 25 installs)
steps.detail: Draft listing copy, a shared-data table matching your scopes, setup documentation and pricing text. Check that all URLs are live and that the app name does not contain 'HubSpot' or 'Hub'.

steps.title: Submit and pass Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: Submit once you have 3 active unaffiliated installs. Initial review within 10 business days, with feedback rounds up to 60 days. The 25-install cap is lifted on approval.

nuances.title: Hard 25-install cap for unlisted marketplace apps
nuances.detail: Enforced on new or migrated Developer Platform apps from 22 September 2025, with no exceptions. Legacy public apps with more than 25 installs get the cap applied automatically when migrated.

nuances.title: Legacy UI app creation is gone
nuances.detail: Legacy public app creation was disabled on 26 May 2026 for new accounts and 23 June 2026 for older accounts. Guides showing 'Apps > Create App' (including composio.dev/auth/hubspot) are out of date. Use Projects + CLI.

nuances.title: AI connectors need user-level permissions to be listed
nuances.detail: The listing requirements name 'AI connectors that don't require user-level permissions' as a rejection reason. Plan for isUserLevel (OAuth only, marked BETA in docs) if you will list an agent product.

nuances.title: Required scopes can block installs on lower tiers
nuances.detail: If an account lacks access to a required scope, the user gets an error at authorization. Put tier-dependent scopes in optionalScopes.

nuances.title: Private distribution is capped at 10 accounts
nuances.detail: Private OAuth apps install only in allowlisted accounts, up to 10 (developer test accounts excluded). It suits internal or design-partner use, not a product.

nuances.title: Only one app under review at a time
nuances.detail: HubSpot automatically rejects any other app you submit while one is under review.

blockers.problem: More than 25 customers need to connect
blockers.whatToDo: Submit for Marketplace listing early, since you only need 3 active installs, or use the Composio-managed HubSpot app until you are listed.

blockers.problem: Can't reach 3 active installs from unaffiliated production accounts
blockers.whatToDo: Onboard design-partner customers under the 25-install allowance first. Your own and test accounts do not count.

blockers.problem: Install fails with scope error on a customer account
blockers.whatToDo: Move tier-specific scopes from requiredScopes to optionalScopes, run hs project upload, and match the Composio scopes.

blockers.problem: Listing rejected for unused scopes, broken URLs or HubSpot branding in the name
blockers.whatToDo: Trim scopes to what the app actually calls, make privacy/support/setup URLs public, and rename the app.

agentCanDo: Map the Composio HubSpot actions you need to required vs optional scopes
Write app-hsmeta.json (redirectUrls, scopes, distribution, auth type)
Run hs project create/upload in a terminal once the developer has authenticated the CLI
Check that the redirect URL and scopes match between HubSpot and Composio, and run a test connection
Draft the listing copy, shared-data table, setup documentation, privacy policy and ToS for Marketplace submission
Check listing URLs are live and the app name follows the branding rules
developerMustDo: Create the HubSpot developer account and authenticate the CLI (hs account auth)
Copy the client secret into Composio
Approve installs as Super Admin in each test or customer account
Get 3 real, unaffiliated customer accounts actively using the app
Submit the listing, accept HubSpot's terms and handle reviewer feedback
redirectUri: Set in redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json, then run hs project upload. At least one is required, and it must use HTTPS; http://localhost is the only exception, for testing. Must use a domain; IP addresses are not supported. The redirect_uri in the authorize and token requests must be one you registered; whether matching is exact is not stated, so treat it as exact (inferred). For Composio, paste the URI shown in the dashboard. composio.dev/auth/hubspot shows https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback, while other Composio docs show a v3.1 path or the older .../api/v1/auth-apps/add.

claims.claim: Marketplace-distribution apps on the Developer Platform are capped at 25 installs until the Marketplace listing is approved, enforced on new or migrated apps from 22 September 2025.
Private-distribution OAuth apps install in up to 10 allowlisted accounts. Static-token apps install in 1 standard account. Developer test accounts are excluded from these counts.
Legacy public app creation was disabled on 26 May 2026 for new accounts and 23 June 2026 for existing accounts. New apps should use the Projects-based platform.
Redirect URLs must use HTTPS, with http://localhost allowed for testing. IP addresses are not supported.
A Marketplace listing needs at least 3 active installs from unique production accounts unaffiliated with you, with activity in the past 30 days.
Initial listing review within 10 business days. The full feedback process should take no more than 60 days. Only one app can be under review at a time.
AI connectors that don't require user-level permissions are listed as a rejection reason.
Installing users must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
Composio offers a managed OAuth app for HubSpot.
Hands-on setup takes 30-60 minutes, and lifting the cap via listing takes about 1-3 months end to end.
